subject: economics
title: Cartels and Competition Policy
welcome_lead: Cartels cheat consumers - regulators fight back.
meta_desc: A-Level Oligopoly: cartels and competition policy.
final_note: Most cartels eventually collapse - but only after damage to consumers.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each cartel member has private incentive to cheat by undercutting the cartel price. Detection requires effort; lenient treatment for whistle-blowers makes the cartel unstable.
The UK CMA and EU Commission investigate cartels and mergers. Fines can reach 10 percent of global turnover; criminal sanctions exist for individuals.
Authorities use concentration ratios and the Herfindahl Index to assess market power. Large mergers that would create dominance can be blocked or required to divest.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between monetary and fiscal policy?
options: QE is when banks charge negative interest on deposits.
Monetary policy uses interest rates and money supply controlled by the central bank; fiscal policy uses government taxation and spending controlled by the Treasury.
Monetary policy is about money and fiscal policy is about taxes.
Both terms mean the same thing — government economic policy.

mcqs.q: Are monopolies always bad for consumers?
options: Monopolies are illegal and always harmful.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
Standard theory says monopolies restrict output and raise prices, but possible benefits include economies of scale, R&D investment and dynamic efficiency.
QE is when banks charge negative interest on deposits.

mcqs.q: How does quantitative easing actually work?
options: QE is when banks charge negative interest on deposits.
QE is the central bank printing money and handing it to citizens.

The central bank creates reserves to buy financial assets (mostly government bonds) from banks and pension funds, raising asset prices and lowering yields — stimulating spending and lending indirectly. It is not literally printing physical cash for the public.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
